body:
Found by the aggregate-vs-raw cross-check gate (PR #314).

## The divergence

`ts_summary_visitor` in `src/compute.c` reads only `f->pid` from the filter. `handle_top_sessions`
(`src/server.c:3688`) guards only on `query_id == 0`.

So a **class-filtered** or **event-filtered** Sessions tab over a window >= 120 s returns
**unfiltered** session numbers — the filter is silently ignored and the user is shown totals for
all wait classes while the UI says one class is selected.

The raw path honours both filters, so the same request answered either way gives different
numbers, and the fast one is wrong.

## Fix — same two options as #317, and they should be decided together

1. Honour class and event filters in `ts_summary_visitor` (the summary record does carry per-event
   totals per session, so this is expressible).
2. Extend `handle_top_sessions`'s guard so a class- or event-filtered request forces the raw path,
   which is the existing precedent in that same handler for `query_id`.

Note this is the *mirror* of #317: there the handler lacked a guard that its siblings had; here the
handler has a guard but only for one of three filter kinds. A consistent rule across
`handle_top_sessions`, `handle_top_events`, `handle_top_queries` and `handle_heatmap` for "which
filters may be served from summaries" would prevent the next instance of this class, and there is
already evidence of per-handler drift: `src/server.c:3741` and `:3762` force raw for Top Queries'
`count` under a class filter and `class_ms` under an event filter, and `:3968` guards the heatmap's
query filter — so three handlers each solved this differently and one did not solve it at all.

Once fixed either way, PR #314's cross-check asserts it automatically.
title: Top Sessions ignores class and event filters on the summary path
